Sandbox_TrekShuttle.Access_tooltip: Multiplayer only. With Owner and crew, the first player to use the shuttle owns it; the owner and admins add and remove crew from the shuttle's right-click menu aboard. With Listed players, only the usernames in Shuttle users may use it. Admins always may, and anyone may always beam down or step out.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.TransporterLimit_too: Multiplayer only. Every beam moves a character a long way at once, which the server's speed anti-cheat counts. Match anti-cheat gives each player 3 charges, one restored every 150 seconds, only when AntiCheatSpeed is set to kick or ban, so players are told the transporter is recharging instead of being kicked. Always unlimited never refuses a beam; use it only with AntiCheatSpeed set to log or disabled.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.SpeedCheck_tooltip: Multiplayer only. Boarding, beaming, the lifts and walking forward to the cockpit each move a player a long way at once, and a server whose AntiCheatSpeed kicks or bans removes ordinary players for it after one or two moves. Relax for the transporter sets AntiCheatSpeed to log while the server runs (the .ini is not changed). Leave it as set keeps the server's setting, and the transporter then rations beams.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.TorpedoFire_tooltip: A photon torpedo sets fire to what it hits, and the fire spreads and burns buildings down. Full is the weapon as designed. Blast only keeps the explosion and the kill but starts no fire at all, for a server that would rather not have its towns burnt. Note that a server which has turned fire off entirely (the NoFire server option) or a safehouse already stops the burning by itself, whichever setting is chosen here.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.Replicator_tooltip: The galley replicator makes any item in the game. Patterns and energy is the shuttle as designed: it can only make something it has scanned a pattern for (scanning is free and gives the item back, and the ship knows its own Starfleet gear from the start), and every replication spends, by the item's weight, from a reserve that is one dilithium crystal burning in the warp core. When it runs dry the ship loads a spare, and when there are no spares the machine stops until somebody finds one. Unrestricted removes both limits: anything in the catalogue, immediately, for nothing. Off leaves the machine in the galley as scenery, and says so when a player tries to use it.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.StartState_tooltip: Cold start: the shuttle is landed near the first player, undamaged and without power. No spare crystals, two probes in the rack. Walk aboard, launch a probe, walk to the dilithium it finds and load it into the warp core, and she comes to life. Commissioned: the shuttle as it has always been, overhead with a full crystal and the spare crystals the balance page gives her. Marooned: a cold start with the shuttle lost. She is down at one of six places in the county, never the one near you, and you have no combadge: no Shuttlecraft menu and no beaming until you have been aboard her once. Annotated maps that mark where she came down turn up where maps do. Only a brand new world is affected: an existing save always carries on as commissioned.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.WildDilithium_toolti: Dilithium crystals lying on natural ground out in the county: fields, woods, dirt and sand, never in town. A tricorder finds them. Plentiful is about one for every 28 by 28 squares of wild ground. Scarce is a quarter of that. Very rare is about one for every 350 by 350 squares. None leaves crystals to probes and loot. A change reaches ground nobody has walked yet.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.EMH_tooltip: The sick bay's holographic doctor: full diagnosis, unlimited treatment for everything a hypospray treats and more, and the only cure for zombie infection in this mod. He draws on the same dilithium reserve the replicator does, and the cure costs a whole crystal and twelve game hours confined to the ship unless the balance page says otherwise. Full is the Doctor as designed. Off leaves the sick bay's wall station inactive and says so. There is deliberately no setting that keeps him and removes the cure. A server owner who does not want the cure turns him off.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.FlightHeight_tooltip: How many storeys up the shuttle hovers when she is taken up. Buildings with fewer storeys pass beneath her; anything as tall or taller is a wall at her height, and she slows to a stop in front of it rather than flying into it. Higher clears more of the map and takes a moment longer to climb to and to come down from.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CommsFirstDay_toolti: How long after the shuttle is commissioned before Lt. Shepard calls a PADD for the first time. On a cold start that is when the first dilithium crystal goes into the warp core; on a commissioned start, the first time anybody boards her. Everything the channel does after that keeps its own spacing from the first call. A week gives a crew time to find the tapes first; straight away is for a server that wants the story from the start.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.PhaserCutting_toolti: Held on a tree, a phaser fells it in a few seconds; held on a door, it burns the door out of its frame whatever is locking it; held on a stump, a rock, a boulder or a bush, it clears it away to build on. Trees, doors and ground is the phaser as designed. Trees and ground keeps it as a woodsman's tool and leaves every lock to keys and crowbars. Off makes it a sidearm and nothing more. Doors and ground in a safehouse a player does not belong to are refused either way.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.HydroponicsWater_too: Crops in the Adirondack's hydroponic trays are watered and kept free of pests and disease by the ship: plant them and harvest them. Off, they need tending like any other crop. Crops planted in the ground are never tended.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.Borg_tooltip: How many of the dead the nanoprobes finished with: assimilated civilians with an eyepiece and a cranial plate, and drones in armour. They walk upright and never run. As common as police is about one zombie in two hundred. A change reaches zombies made after the world is next loaded; the dead already walking keep what they are.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CaptainTruth_tooltip: When Captain Titus, on the Adirondack's bridge, will tell a player what her people believe caused the plague. Until then she tells them everything else and says there is more. 'When it is earned' is once Shepard has told it on the channel, or the player has watched Shepard's last log, or has brought two of the crew home.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CaptainTruth_option1: Only once Shepard has told it
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.AdirondackAccess_too: Whether the shuttle's transporter can reach the U.S.S. Adirondack from the start. Earned: the crew bring her people home, recover three pattern enhancers and hold a transporter lock, and each player passes the Doctor's biofilter screening. Rescues only: the rescues alone. A world that had already been aboard her keeps its access.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.AdirondackRescues_to: How many downed crew the ship has to bring home before the Adirondack will spend a transporter lock on the players.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.Raids_tooltip: How often Captain Titus asks for help when the transporter's pattern buffer overflows. A request comes only to players the Adirondack can beam aboard, and lasts five hours; accepting beams you to the fight and home again after. Frequent brings the first request an hour after a player is cleared.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.RaidSize_tooltip: How many of the dead a raid's pattern buffer holds.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.BeamUp_tooltip: Off: nobody beams up to the shuttle from the ground. They walk aboard through the hatch of a landed shuttle, and call it down to do so. Beaming down is never refused, so nobody is shut in.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.Flight_tooltip: Off: the shuttle cannot be taken up. It is still driven on the ground, called down and sent back up.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.ShipWeapons_tooltip: What the shuttle's seats may fire. The tractor beam is not a weapon and is not affected. Hand phasers and the rest of the armoury follow the server's own PvP rules.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.Shields_tooltip: Off: the landed shuttle has no shields, and the helm cannot raise them.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.DistressCalls_toolti: Off: the ship hears no distress calls, so there is nobody to rescue. Rank and the Adirondack's clearance are both earned by rescues: with this off, set Adirondack access to Open from the start or Closed.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.Installations_toolti: Off: a warp core, replicator or EMH station kit cannot be installed in a building. Machines already installed stay and work.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.PowerUse_tooltip: How fast dilithium is used by everything that draws on it, on top of the costs below. None: a ship with power never runs down, though a dark ship still needs its first crystal. Menus show the cost before this setting; the note after a charge says what was really spent.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.AccessUsers_tooltip: Usernames, separated by semicolons (alice;bob). Used when Who may use the shuttle is Listed players: only they, and admins, may use the shared shuttle.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CabinStyle_tooltip: Whose hands built the inside of a ship: its bulkheads, its deck and every fitting. Her hull's gives a Starfleet shuttle a Starfleet cabin, a Klingon raider a Klingon one and a Vulcan ring ship a Vulcan one. Decided once, when a ship's cabin is first built, and hers for good: changing this later changes only cabins not built yet.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CabinLayout_tooltip: Shuffled: each ship's galley, sink and sick bay cabinet stand in an order of their own along her port bulkhead, so no two cabins are quite the same. Standard: every cabin is the same one. Decided once, when a ship's cabin is first built.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CabinGalley_tooltip: The stasis unit, the range, and the ship's rations in the cupboard under the sink. Off, a new cabin has none of them: its crew find their own food. The replicator has its own setting. Decided once, when a ship's cabin is first built.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CabinWater_tooltip: The galley sink makes its own water and never runs dry. Off, a new cabin's sink is a dry cupboard. Decided once, when a ship's cabin is first built.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CabinMedical_tooltip: The sick bay's cabinet, with its Starfleet medical set, and the biobed. Off, a new cabin has neither. The Doctor has his own setting. Decided once, when a ship's cabin is first built.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.PersonalShuttles_too: None: one shuttle, shared. Every player: each player also has a shuttle of their own, with its own cabin, stores and power, waiting overhead to be called down. Listed players: only the usernames in Personal shuttle users have one. The owner of a personal shuttle adds crew from its menu aboard. The shared shuttle stays, and Who may use the shuttle still decides who may use it.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.PersonalShuttleUsers: Usernames, separated by semicolons. Used when Personal shuttles is Listed players.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.AdirondackUsers_tool: Usernames, separated by semicolons. Empty: everybody who meets Adirondack access. Otherwise only these players, and admins, may beam aboard, and they still have to meet Adirondack access.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.AdirondackName: Name of the ship in orbit
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.AdirondackName_toolt: What the U.S.S. Adirondack is called in menus, notes, the channel, the Captain's and the crew's talk. Tapes played on the television, item names and this settings page keep the original name: a lore pack replaces those (SERVERS.md).

Sandbox_TrekShuttle.LootDilithiumMin: Dilithium in a town's loot: fewest
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.LootDilithiumMin_too: The county is counted in districts 1,500 squares across, about a town each: Muldraugh, Rosewood, Riverside and March Ridge are one apiece, Louisville half a dozen. Every container in a district, between them, gives up a number of crystals between this and the most, drawn once for each district when the world is made. Crystals still turn up where they did: gem cases, electronics shelves, tool crates. Both at 0: none in loot at all. A change reaches containers not yet looted; crystals already found are not taken back.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.LootDilithiumMax: Dilithium in a town's loot: most
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.LootDilithiumMax_too: The most crystals one district's containers give up. See the setting above. The same number as the fewest makes every district the same.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.ProbeFind_tooltip: How many probes in a hundred come back with a dilithium fix. The first probe of a save always finds something, and a long enough run of empty ones is followed by a find: six at 30, two at 90. At 0 only that first probe ever finds any. A probe costs what Cost: other systems makes it.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.RaidCrystal: Raid crates with a crystal (per cent)
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.RaidCrystal_tooltip: The chance that a raid's outpost has a dilithium crystal in one of its crates.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.StartCrystals: Spare crystals at a commissioned start
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.StartCrystals_toolti: How many spare crystals a shuttle that starts commissioned has in her warp core, beside the one burning. Read once, when a ship's cabin is first built. A cold or marooned shuttle has none, and a personal shuttle has none.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CostReplicator_toolt: What a replication costs, as a percentage of the mod's own price. At 100 a crystal is 5,000 units and a bandage costs 25, a tin of beans 60, a hammer 120 and a shotgun 220. 200 doubles every price, 50 halves it, 0 makes replication free. The panel shows the price this gives.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CostTransporter_tool: What a beam costs, each way, for each person: 75 units at 100. The hatch is a door and is always free. 0 makes beaming free.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CostFlight_tooltip: Calling her down (400 units at 100), sending her up (150), starting her engine (50), taking off (300), every square driven (1.5) or flown (4), and every game minute in the air (3). At 100 a crystal is about one outing with the shuttle. 0 makes all of it free.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CostShields_tooltip: Each zombie the shields push away (5 units at 100) and each point of crash damage they mend (3). 0 makes the shields free.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CostWeapons_tooltip: A photon torpedo (250 units at 100), each bolt of the ship's phasers (15) and each second of the tractor beam (10). Hand phasers draw nothing from the ship. 0 makes them free.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CostMedical_tooltip: Projecting the Emergency Medical Hologram (300 units at 100), a treatment (100), a detox (400) and the biofilter screening (150). The cure for infection is counted in crystals, below.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CostSystems_tooltip: Fabricating a probe (1,500 units at 100), recharging a perimeter sentry (750), an android's charge while asleep aboard, and the galley's fridge and range.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CureCrystals_tooltip: How many spare dilithium crystals the Doctor's cure for zombie infection takes, spent when the treatment starts. 0: the cure costs only the time.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.CureHours_tooltip: How many game hours the patient must stay aboard for the cure to finish. Leaving the ship, or the ship losing power, ends the treatment and keeps the crystals.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.Shuttles_tooltip: Off: there is no shuttle on this server. None is set down or issued, nobody has the Shuttlecraft menu, and nothing can be asked of one left standing from before. Anybody aboard one may still leave. The things she would have issued then turn up in the world's loot instead (Items in the world's loot, below). The ship in orbit is reached by the shuttle's transporter, so with this off she is out of reach as well.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.Adirondack_tooltip: Off: the U.S.S. Adirondack is not there. Nobody beams aboard her but an admin, she never calls a PADD, and there are no distress calls, rescues or raids.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.FieldStation_tooltip: Off: no breaker box is hung in Muldraugh, and the Starfleet station under it cannot be entered. A box already on the wall stays, and opens on nothing.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.Aliens_tooltip: Off: no alien species may be picked for a character, a character who has one loses it as with the species' own settings, and none of the dead are Borg. Things aliens made, the bat'leth among them, are items and have their own switches below.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.ItemLoot: Items in the world's loot (per cent)
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.ItemLoot_tooltip: Only when Shuttles is off, so that there is no ship to issue them. The chance that a container in a fitting kind of room holds one of the mod's things that is switched on below: weapons in gun stores, police and army stores and pawn shops, the medical set in pharmacies and hospitals, the field kit, instruments and installation kits in tool stores and garages, uniforms in clothing stores, bottles in bars, seeds in garden stores. 0: none.
Sandbox_TrekShuttle.ItemBatleth_tooltip: Off: no new Bat'leth is issued in a ship's lockers, made by a replicator or found in the world's loot. One a player already has is theirs to keep.
